newsitem.title: USA: July turns hot for sales of U.S. mutual funds.
newsitem.headline: July turns hot for sales of U.S. mutual funds.

text.p: After a summer slumber in June, July has proven to be a hot month for sales of mutual funds, U.S. fund companies said Wednesday.
Record gains on the stock market, low inflation, strong corporate earnings and a budget deal in Washington incited investors to pump cash into stock funds in July, they said.
"July is proving to be an extraordinary month," said Brian Mattes, a spokesman for mutual fund company Vanguard Group. "Stock funds here are showing their second strongest month this year."

The mutual fund trade group Investment Company Institute said Wednesday that cash flows into stock mutual funds in June, historically the beginning of a slow spell for the industry, fell to $16.59 billion from $20.54 billion in May.
At the beginning of June, the markets were volatile with fears of an impending hike in U.S. interest rates and nervousness over upcoming second-quarter earnings.
What a difference a month makes.

The Dow Jones industrial average barrelled above the 8,000 level for the first time in July, and last week Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan was uncharacteristically upbeat about the U.S. economy in testimony before the Senate.
"The extraordinary bullish market no doubt is a primary reason for the strong inflows into the stock funds," Mattes said.
In addition, the White House and Republicans mended their differences and came to an agreement on a balanced budget, and second-quarter corporate profits generally were stronger than expected.
Vanguard expects net flows of nearly $4.3 billion in July into stock funds, up from $2.2 billion in June, but shy of the record $4.9 billion in January, Mattes said.
Flows into international funds were also strong at Vanguard during the month, totalling $417 million vs. $248 million in June, he said.
Boston-based Fidelity Investments, the largest mutual fund company in the world, said it expected flows of more than $2 billion into stock funds in July vs. $1 billion in June.
"Contrary to historic slowdowns in the summmer months ... investors stayed in the market," said spokeswoman Robyn Tice.
Growth and income funds and index funds have been among the strongest categories among stock funds, she said.
Flows into bond funds appeared to be mixed in July.
Vanguard Group said flows into taxable and tax-free bond funds rose sharply in July. However, Fidelity reported redemptions in its bond funds.
Charles Schwab, which sells thousands of mutual funds through its Mutual Fund Marketplace, said that its sales of bond funds slowed but were positive in July.

The ICI said flows into bond and income funds in June saw net inflows of $2.11 billion, down slightly from inflows of $2.75 billion in May. Money market funds had a net inflow of $1.21 billion in June, compared with $10.24 billion in inflows in May, the ICI said.
